items.title: ggml/llama.cpp releases: b10353
items.description:
<details open>

ggml : require contiguous src for ROLL on CUDA and Metal (#25928)

ggml_roll only asserts nb[0] == ggml_type_size, so a permuted src is a
valid input, but the CUDA and Metal roll kernels index by ne alone and
never read the nb strides. A non-contiguous src therefore produced
silently
items.summary: A recent update to ggml/llama.cpp enforces contiguous source data for the ROLL operation on CUDA and Metal to prevent silent errors, addressing a potential issue where non-contiguous sources could lead to incorrect computations without proper validation. This change is crucial for ensuring numerical accuracy across different hardware implementations.
items.summary_detailed: The ggml/llama.cpp project released an update addressing an issue where non-contiguous source data could be accepted by the `ggml_roll` function, leading to silent errors on CUDA and Metal kernels. This fix ensures that only contiguous source data is accepted for these operations. The broader impact includes improved reliability and correctness of models running on GPU-accelerated environments.
items.summary_bullets:
• ggml requires contiguous source for ROLL on CUDA and Metal
• The CUDA and Metal roll kernels do not check source data contiguity
• Non-contiguous source can lead to silent errors in these kernels
